environment.build: Rust dev/test with local Qt 6.11.2; offline workspace checks
environment.native_test: Qt Quick/WebEngine offscreen fixture; CTest native_insert executable
environment.wayland: WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1 was present; no Wayland or physical-keyboard qualification was run
environment.scope: ApplicationWorld document identity, QML same-document qualification, BrowserUi restore leases and cleanup; no full native BrowserUi navigation lifecycle fixture

baseline_comparison.result: Before the navigation lifecycle change, the three new NativeTabContent identity/restore component cases failed while the other 114 QML tests passed. After the change, the full QML suite passed with 118 tests.

observations: The native_insert CTest executable passed. Existing production event-filter regressions cover page-owned keydown, repeat and release routing across policy/epoch changes, overlapping keys, stale-release replacement, and browser-owned repeat routing after a page mapping change.
The ApplicationWorld document identity is isolated from MainWorld, remains stable through history.pushState and fragment changes, and differs after replacement with a new document.
Qt emitted no main-frame navigation request for the pushState and fragment URL changes in the fixture.

A same-document notification carries the expected tab, document token, destination URL, and input epoch. A document mismatch completes without a restorable identity, and a deferred probe callback is ignored after navigation start.

test_results.command: cargo xtask test engine ran the native_insert fixture, which does not instantiate BrowserUi and a WebEngine tab to exercise the complete pass-through restore lifecycle.
test_results.reason: The tests do not end-to-end verify actual persistent Pass Through restoration, Pass Next Key cancellation, reload, renderer death, and tab-switch reset through the BrowserUi navigation callbacks.

observations: The existing native fixture preserves the owner of held page and browser gestures across policy and input-epoch changes. It does not change focus to a different WebEngine recipient and test the next physical gesture there.
All workspace Rust tests passed, including 413 engine unit tests, along with config, core, runtime, storage, application, and xtask suites.
All 118 QML/WebEngine tests passed, including the existing hint, focus, recovery, and interaction regressions.
The native_insert CTest executable passed with 100% of its reported tests passing.

test_results.command: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo xtask check --locked --offline; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked --offline -- -D warnings
observations: Formatting and strict workspace Clippy passed with warnings denied. The xtask check also passed generated-contract validation, the release artifact manifest (38 checked-in inputs), and license policy (11 locked dependencies).

remaining_risks: The full BrowserUi same-document pass-through restore and real navigation/reload/renderer/tab-switch exits are not qualified by a native end-to-end fixture.
T027's held-gesture owner regression does not switch focus to a different WebEngine recipient and verify the next fresh physical gesture.
No Wayland, physical keyboard, or IME qualification was run.
not_run_reasons: T026 native-qt-offscreen: the current native_insert fixture exercises gesture ownership but does not compose BrowserUi navigation identity, BrowserUi mode restoration, and a live WebEngine tab.
